title: Review of c43's CIPS consumer (fresh seed 1717): S, X and E reproduce (frozen 82-droplet twin vs 74 prey splits; all 35 consumers gone within 100 t of the prey cut), but the consumer is a band on its prey (93% of consumer bodies touch prey, 57% of their area inside it, 7% free) that divides only with its prey (3 strict splits vs labkit's 30): I and D for the consumer are not held
summary: Fresh-seed labkit re-runs of the claimed world (seed 1717, 128^2, t=12000, --lineage-k 5), its consumer-free twin (pred_on 0) and its prey-removal fork (tcut 3000). The prey population with consumers divides (74 prey persistent splits, generation 8) while the twin is a frozen hexagonal emulsion of 82 droplets (10 splits, generation 1): X reproduces. The fork: consumers 35 at t=3000 -> 0 at t=3100, max q 1.03 -> 0.14 -> 0.08 (bath), while the fed run keeps 30-35: E reproduces, and the consumer's dependence on prey is dynamical (its condensation needs the catalysis that eats prey), not built in. But attach.py finds that over t >= 2000, 93% of consumer body-frames touch a prey droplet, 57% of their area lies inside prey and 7% are free; the strict strip test (splits3.py, channel 1, area >= 8) finds 3 consumer splits, all with prey alongside (s1717_cons.png), against labkit's 30 persistent splits. The consumer is a self-made layer of a prey-consumer composite that divides when the prey pinches, so I and D are not held for it.

observations.S: rerun/pack/seed1717/sheet.jpg t=0: unstructured field; prey and consumer bands by t=500
observations.X: rerun/twin/seed1717/sheet.jpg (82 static prey, 10 persistent splits, generation 1) vs rerun/pack/seed1717/metrics.json prey 74 persistent splits, generation 8, 41 prey at the end
observations.E: attach.txt: fork consumers 35 (t=3000) -> 0 (t=3100), max q 0.14 -> 0.08 bath, while rerun/pack keeps 30-35 consumers; the dependence comes from the catalysis that condenses q, not from a term building q from prey

against.I: attach.txt: 93% of consumer body-frames touch prey, mean 57% of consumer area inside prey, 7% free; rerun/pack/seed1717/sheet.jpg shows consumers as bands on prey edges
against.D: s1717_cons.png: 3 strict consumer splits (both daughters >= 8 px, 5 frames), all as the prey under them pinches; labkit's 30 consumer persistent splits (generation 3) count the composite's splits

seeds_run.result: pass for S, X, E; I and D fail as before

controls_run.X: rerun/twin/seed1717 (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration, lineage window)
controls_run.E: rerun/efork/seed1717 (tcut 3000) with rerun/pack/seed1717 as the fed twin

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; the E fork removes all prey at once, which also removes the substrate the bands sit on, so it shows dependence on prey but not a per-body metabolic budget; I did not test a local, single-body prey cut.
